source: Amirnet Tier 1 (A2, CEFR-J v1.5) headwords, data/amirnet-vocab.csv. Missing-from-bank list recomputed live by diffing every Tier 1 headword against every existing data/generated/batch-*.jsonl headword before writing. 40 alphabetical, single-word, unambiguous Tier 1 entries: comparative, convenience (both genuinely missing gaps found alphabetically BEFORE the 'cooker' marker left by batch-2026-09-13.jsonl's manifest — verified against data/amirnet-vocab.csv and every existing batch file, not multi-word/slash-variant/inflection-only entries, so written now rather than left as a silent gap), then cooker, cooking, cooler, correctly, countryside, creativity, cricket, crisp, crowded, crown, cruise, cupboard, curry, curse, cycling, dam, dancer, daylight, dentist, dessert, developed, diamond, diary, dinosaur, disadvantage, disappointed, disappointing, disco, dishonest, dislike, dizzy, done, download, downstairs, downtown, drawer, drawing, dressed. One deliberate substitution: the CSV lists 'done' with pos 'do-verb', which is not a value gateSense's POS_VALUES accepts (noun|verb|adjective|adverb|preposition|conjunction|pronoun|determiner|interjection) and is not a standard part-of-speech tag at all — 'done' was written as pos 'adjective' for its common predicative sense ('finished/cooked completely', e.g. 'Is the chicken done?'), which is both grammatically accurate and CEFR-A2-appropriate; flagged here rather than decided silently.
selection_rule: Tier 1 (A2), skipping multi-word entries, slash-spelling-variant entries (e.g. 'apologize/apologise') and headwords already present in the bank, alphabetical order. A live diff (Node script, not memory) found 'comparative' and 'convenience' had been skipped by earlier batches despite being eligible — included here to close that gap. Next marker for the following tick (measured live after this batch, alphabetical among remaining eligible single-word Tier 1 entries): 'drill'.
quota_rule: No per-batch ceiling (plan/25-content-commissions.md K-005, Roy 09/09; spotCheckPlan() runs per batch FILE per scripts/build-ingest-sql.mjs:159, confirmed again by this tick's own scheduling prompt, which named the historical 12-row batches an over-read of the old whole-bank ISO 2859-1 ceiling and asked for a batch size chosen and justified rather than defaulted). Batch size = 40, roughly double the largest prior batch (30, C-0545): chosen because this tick had direct Node/TypeScript access to import the real gateSense and run it against the full draft before writing a single row to the tracked batch file (same method as lesson 40/plan/80-content-lessons.md, via a scratch script under .scratch/, not committed) rather than working from memory of the rules, which is what let per-item verification scale past the 20-30 row range that recent ticks found was the hand-checking limit without that tooling. Every row went through: (1) the real gateSense on the full draft, (2) a dedicated token-level scan of every non-target word in every distractor's stem-substitution for accidental validity (lessons 6/17/23/24), (3) a mechanical a/an-agreement scan between fixed articles before a blank and every distractor's initial sound, and (4) the 7-case negative control from lesson 40. The bottleneck was still per-item human/model judgment on distractor quality, not the mechanical gate — see 'note' below for what that caught.
note: R-014 (replaced 10/09): no human sample-review queue; 38/40 rows carry translation_confidence = 'high', 2/40 (comparative, crisp) carry 'medium' — comparative (צורת ההשוואה is the accurate grammar-register translation but this headword is itself a meta-linguistic/grammar term rather than a concrete A2 object, flagged for register fit rather than translation accuracy), crisp (צ'יפס is the colloquial Israeli-Hebrew word for this exact British snack but is ambiguous with the more common meaning 'fries/chips' in everyday Hebrew usage) — flagged rather than asserted, per policy. gateSense (lib/core/contentSchema.ts) ran directly against all 40 rows before writing, via a scratch validator script (.scratch/checkgate.mjs, not committed) that imports the real gateSense and the real data/generated/allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt: first pass was 24/40 (16 rows failed, overwhelmingly on level drift from an everyday supporting word not present in the NGSL-derived allowed-words surface-form list — e.g. 'bat', 'witch', 'gracefully', 'app', 'internet', 'socks', 'pencil', 'classroom', 'shone', 'Japan' [also a banned proper noun], 'Saturday' [banned day name], 'three' [banned spelled-out number above one] — plus one stem over the 14-word limit and one quoted "'-er'" tokenizing as a bare drift hit); every failing sentence was rewritten with an allowed-words-checked substitute and a second pass ran 40/40 clean. Beyond the mechanical gate, a full stem-substitution printout (every semantic distractor inserted into every one of its item's three stems, read in full) caught three accidental-validity issues the gate cannot see: (a) 'dinosaur' distractor 'elephant' after a fixed 'a ____' produced the grammatically self-revealing "a elephant" — swapped to 'camel'; a systematic a/an-agreement scan against all 120 distractor-stem pairs found no other instance; (b) 'convenience' L1/L3 stems allowed 'a real beauty' (an English idiom praising appearance) and a generic 'made up for that' to read as plausibly true with the 'beauty'/'safety' distractors instead of the target — both stems rewritten to hinge specifically on proximity/location, which only 'convenience' answers; (c) 'dressed' stems built around 'in a warm coat' let both distractors ('covered', 'wrapped') read as equally natural near-synonyms for bundling up in a coat — rewritten around a job-interview frame, where 'covered'/'wrapped' for an interview read as clearly wrong. A 7-item negative control (one deliberately broken row per failure mode: level drift, leaked answer, Latin letters in translation, fewer than 4 scorable distractors, missing blank, nikud in translation, headword missing from example), built on the 'cooker' row from this batch, ran through the same real gate: 0/7 passed, confirming the gate still discriminates. ⚠️ OPEN FINDING, carried unchanged from C-0545/C-0563 and not decided here: gateSense does not check distractor words against allowedWords at all; distractors here were kept to simple, common A1/A2 English words by manual judgment (not checked against the NGSL-derived allowed-words list), for the reason C-0545 gave — that list predates the CEFR-J headword source and PM/DEV have not ruled on a replacement. npm run build:ingest, npm run build:levels, npm run measure:gate and npm run build:preview all ran clean over the full bank after writing — see the commit for the exact row/file counts. No number is written as a word above 'one' and no proper name appears in any example or item stem.
